text: Every earlier chapter governed data that stays inside one metastore. Delta Sharing is what happens when data needs to leave that boundary — and the key fact is that it doesn't leave governance behind.

Three objects work together. A share is a named, owned, auditable collection of tables — a securable object just like a catalog or a table. A recipient is the identity allowed to read it. And GRANT ON SHARE is the privilege that actually connects the two.

CREATE SHARE makes the container. ALTER SHARE ADD TABLE puts a table in it — here, a curated customer summary, already masked. WITH HISTORY is a deliberate choice: it lets the recipient run time-travel queries and streaming reads against the shared table, not just a one-time snapshot.

CREATE RECIPIENT USING ID sets up Databricks-to-Databricks sharing using the partner's own metastore ID — no token management required. Leave off USING ID and you get a token-based recipient instead, for consumers who can't authenticate as a Databricks metastore.

GRANT SELECT ON SHARE TO RECIPIENT connects them. SHOW GRANTS ON SHARE answers the audit question: who can see this outside our metastore right now? And REVOKE cuts access off immediately — there's no lingering copy sitting on a partner's server, because sharing reads live, governed data.

The habits from earlier chapters still apply right up to this new perimeter. Share a view that already has a column mask or row filter applied, not the raw table — and share only the minimum the business case actually needs.

A share is a Unity Catalog object, permissioned and auditable like everything else in this course. Next lesson: governing machine learning assets — the same permission model, applied to a model registry instead of a table.
